findings.summary: D179 says planner_timeout_s stays the same on a revision call. This change makes that line out of date, and the plan neither notes it nor reports it as a follow-up.
findings.evidence: docs/decisions.md:5180 reads 'A revision call may cost more and run longer, and `planner_usd` and `planner_timeout_s` are unchanged.' After this change, a revision that raises the effort runs with twice planner_timeout_s. Criterion 4 keeps decisions.md unchanged, so the record will contradict the code. The plan's dependents list does not mention D179. Fix: Keep decisions.md unchanged, as the reading requires. Have the CHANGELOG bullet say that it partly supersedes D179's tradeoff on the time limit. Also report in the producer's output that D179 needs a follow-up decision note.
findings.location: docs/decisions.md:5180 (D179 Tradeoff); plan step 6 / CHANGELOG entry

findings.summary: With the live settings the change does almost nothing. The plan says so, but the operators' audience should hear it plainly in the CHANGELOG.
findings.evidence: athena.toml:224 sets planner_timeout_s = 86400, so the 606 s case that motivated this work only happens under short limits, such as the 600 s in the test fixtures. Step 6 already plans to say 'the live limit is 86400 so it matters for short limits'. Fix: Keep that sentence in the CHANGELOG bullet. Do not drop it during editing.

summary: I checked the plan against planning.rs, config.rs and tests.rs; it is sound and fits one producer run. I read planning_round (planning.rs:83-189): deadline_s is set from cfg.planner_timeout_s at line 137 and the agent_spec timeout at line 163. The model and effort are chosen at lines 144-148, using only values already in scope before the brief is built at line 129, so moving that block earlier is safe. Models::planner_revision_setting (config.rs:380-396) returns the key's effort only when it ranks at or above the current effort. Otherwise it returns the current effort unchanged. So comparing the returned effort string with the planner's own effort detects exactly a raise, with no second copy of the ranking rule. Using the scaled value for both deadline_s and the spec keeps true the rule pinned by the test at tests.rs:1437 (the brief's stated deadline equals the enforced timeout). That test runs round 1 only, so it stays green. The test seam exists: run_for_revision's Script closure (tests.rs:1559) can record spec.timeout the same way tests.rs:1450-1453 already does. The fixture sets planner_timeout_s = 600 (tests.rs:1516) and planner effort high, so the planned cases are correct: xhigh gives 1200 s; unset, medium and high give 600 s. Each would fail if the scaling were unconditional or missing. Grep finds no other code that reads planner_timeout_s besides config validation and its tests. No external service is called, and no athena.toml field is added. The only finding is minor: D179 in docs/decisions.md becomes out of date, and decisions.md is out of scope, so the CHANGELOG should note it.
